_comment: Data layers compared between Earth sites and Moon/Mars targets. Each layer is read from data/layers/<id>/<site_id>.tif (any CRS, any resolution). normalize: none = compare raw values (scale in layer units); zscore = compare shape of the distribution (scale in standard deviations); minmax = compare 2-98 percentile-stretched values (scale 0-1). score = exp(-Wasserstein distance / scale). See docs/DATA_INTEGRATION.md. source_ids link each body's data to an entry in config/data_sources.json (used by the source filter).

layers.label: Day-night temperature swing
layers.description: How much the surface temperature changes between day and night. Earth: MODIS mean (day - night) at the ~10:30 / 22:30 overpasses, June-August. Moon: Diviner max - min over a full lunar day in southern summer. Mars: THEMIS afternoon minus pre-dawn, northern summer. The bodies differ by 10-100x, so sites are scored by the ratio of their typical (median) swing.

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MOD11A2 (LST_Day_1km - LST_Night_1km, Jun-Aug)
sources.mars: Mars Odyssey THEMIS projected brightness temperature (ASU / NASA PDS): mean afternoon (12-17 h) minus mean pre-dawn (0-7 h), northern summer
sources.moon: LRO Diviner 240 m south-polar temperatures (Williams et al. 2019), via UCLA / PDS

layers.label: How cold (typical temperature)
layers.description: Typical surface temperature: the mean of the site's typical low and high (data/facts/temperature/). Earth: MODIS summer night and day. Moon: Diviner coldest and hottest over a lunar day. Mars: THEMIS early morning and late afternoon. Every Earth site is far warmer than Mars and the Moon, so each Earth site is scored against the other Earth sites: the coldest scores 1.0, the warmest 0.0. Together with the day-night swing this makes up the Temperature category (half weight each).

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MOD11A2 (mean of LST_Night_1km and LST_Day_1km, Jun-Aug)
sources.mars: Mars Odyssey THEMIS: mean of early-morning and late-afternoon brightness temperature, northern summer
sources.moon: LRO Diviner 240 m south-polar temperatures: mean of the coldest and hottest over a lunar day

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MCD43A3 (white-sky shortwave albedo)
sources.moon: NASA PDS: LRO LOLA normal albedo

layers.label: Barren ground (no vegetation)
layers.description: Share of the site where even peak-summer NDVI stays below 0.2: bare rock, sand, ice or water. The Moon and Mars have no vegetation, so their share is 100% by definition.

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: MODIS/061/MOD13A2 (max NDVI, Jun-Aug)

layers.label: Surface dust / fine soil
layers.description: Share of the site covered by fine dust or fine soil. Earth: bare ground whose topsoil is mostly silt + clay (> 50%). Mars: TES Dust Cover Index below 0.94 (dust-covered surface, Ruff & Christensen 2002). The two are measured differently (soil texture vs thermal-infrared emissivity), so each body has its own threshold. Moon: no data yet.

sources.earth: Google Earth Engine: OpenLandMap topsoil sand content (fine = 100 - sand) on barren ground (MODIS MOD13A2 NDVI < 0.2)
sources.mars: TES Dust Cover Index (Ruff & Christensen 2002), numeric 16 pixels/degree map from ASU
sources.moon: No comparable surface dust map. Scout v3 LDEX orbital dust profiles and Diviner modeled rock cover are displayed separately; neither is surface dust coverage.

layers.label: Radar circular polarization ratio
layers.description: Surface roughness / ice indicator from compact- or hybrid-polarimetry radar.

sources.moon: NASA PDS: LRO Mini-RF CPR mosaics

layers.label: Topographic position (demo)
layers.description: Elevation relative to the surrounding 2 km mean. Generated from the DEMs by scripts/make_demo_layers.py only to test the layer pipeline; it is not independent data.
